name: Kathmandu
kicker: Temples, bazaars, and the first road out of the valley
summary: The hop begins in the Kathmandu Valley — Boudha, Durbar squares, and the highway or runway west. Most Nepal journeys still start here, even if the night is short.
details: Boudhanath kora at dusk before an early bus
Thamel gear run for ABC if you are continuing up
Hotel pickup for tourist bus or TIA domestic flight

name: Pokhara
kicker: Phewa light, Sarangkot dawn, gateway to Annapurna
summary: Pokhara is the pause between highway and Himalaya. Lakeside boats, paragliding, and the last hot shower before the ABC trail. Most hops west end — or begin again — here.
details: Sunrise at Sarangkot over Machhapuchhre
Phewa Lake boat to the Tal Barahi shrine
Paragliding or a quiet walk to the Peace Pagoda

name: Annapurna Base Camp
kicker: Stone steps, hot springs, and a 4,130 m amphitheatre of ice
summary: ABC is not a road hop — it is a walking hop. From Nayapul or Ghandruk you climb through Gurung villages, bamboo, and the sanctuary to a cirque of Annapurna I, Hiunchuli, and Fishtail.
details: Ghandruk village and Gurung Museum
Jhinu Danda hot springs after a long descent
Sunrise at ABC with Annapurna South in the bowl

name: Lumbini
kicker: Maya Devi Temple, monasteries, and the quiet Terai plain
summary: Lumbini is where Siddhartha Gautama was born — a UNESCO site of temples, monasteries from twenty nations, and the Maya Devi garden. Most hops arrive from Kathmandu by highway through Chitwan country or a short flight to Bhairahawa.
details: Maya Devi Temple and the Ashoka pillar
Monastic zone walk — Thai, Chinese, Korean, and German temples
Crane sanctuary and cycling the flat Terai lanes

name: Chitwan National Park
kicker: Jeep safari, canoe, and Tharu villages on the Terai
summary: Chitwan is Nepal’s classic wildlife stop — one-horned rhinos, crocodiles, and if you are lucky, a Bengal tiger from a jeep or canoe. Most hops arrive from Kathmandu via Mugling and Narayangarh; Sauraha is the main lodge base on the Rapti river.
details: Half-day jeep safari in Chitwan National Park
Rapti river canoe at dawn for birds and gharial
Tharu cultural dance and village walk in the evening

name: Everest Base Camp
kicker: Lukla runway, Sherpa villages, and the Khumbu glacier at 5,364 m
summary: The most famous walk on Earth. Fly into Lukla, climb through Namche and Tengboche, and stand under Everest, Nuptse, and Lhotse at base camp — then watch sunrise from Kala Patthar. Twelve to fourteen days, two acclimatisation stops, and no road anywhere.
details: Namche Bazaar Saturday market and the Everest View Hotel terrace
Tengboche monastery with Ama Dablam in the window
Kala Patthar sunrise over Everest, Nuptse, and Pumori

name: Poon Hill
kicker: Three thousand stone steps, rhododendron forest, and a 3,210 m sunrise
summary: Nepal’s most popular short trek — three to five days from Pokhara through Ulleri’s stone stairs and Ghorepani’s rhododendron forest to a dawn panorama of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, and Machhapuchhre. No altitude worries, real villages, and a loop back through Ghandruk.
details: Sunrise from the Poon Hill view tower over Dhaulagiri and Annapurna
Ghorepani rhododendron forest in full March–April bloom
Gurung and Magar villages — Ulleri, Ghandruk, Tadapani

name: Jomsom & Muktinath
season: Oct — Nov · Mar — May · walkable in monsoon
kicker: The world’s deepest gorge, apple orchards, and a temple at 3,710 m
summary: Fly twenty minutes from Pokhara or drive a day up the Kali Gandaki gorge into a high-altitude desert that looks like Tibet. Jomsom is the hub, Marpha the apple village, Kagbeni the gate to Upper Mustang, and Muktinath the temple both Hindus and Buddhists climb to.
details: Muktinath’s 108 water spouts and the eternal flame
Kagbeni’s mud-walled alleys at the edge of Upper Mustang
Marpha apple brandy and whitewashed Thakali houses

name: Langtang Valley
kicker: The closest Himalayan valley to Kathmandu — Tamang villages, yak cheese, and 7,000 m walls
summary: One long bus day north of Kathmandu, then three walking days up a forested gorge to Kyanjin Gompa under Langtang Lirung. Fewer trekkers than Everest or Annapurna, a rebuilt village with a story, and two ridge climbs above 4,700 m that need no permit beyond the park fee.
details: Kyanjin Gompa monastery and the 1955 Swiss-built cheese factory
Tserko Ri or Kyanjin Ri for glaciers and Langtang Lirung
Langtang village memorial and Tamang tea houses

name: Nagarkot
kicker: Bhaktapur’s squares on the way up, the Himalaya at dawn on the ridge
summary: The easiest famous hop in Nepal — an afternoon in Bhaktapur’s medieval Durbar Square, a night at 2,175 m on the valley rim, and a sunrise that stretches from Langtang to a distant tip of Everest on a clear morning. Bus, taxi, bike, or a hike from Changu Narayan.
details: Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Nyatapola, and juju dhau curd
Dawn from the Nagarkot view tower — Langtang to Everest
Ridge hike to Changu Narayan or Dhulikhel
